messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Confusion in glmer poisson models
parts:
Hi!

I am quite confused as to what rstnarm does when doing a Poisson log-link regression using stan_glmer.

I have written the respective Stan program as I think it should match, but it apparently does not line up. Any hints on what is the difference between the rstanarm model and what I wrote up in the stan model would be great.

Attached are the files which run out of the box, but for the lazy I paste code below.

Thanks!
Sebastian

counts <- data.frame(r=c(5,2,7), e=c(10, 34, 51), study=1:3)

## fit Poisson (log-link) hierarchical model with tau ~ Exp(-3) and
## intercept ~ N(0,1)
poisson_arm <- stan_glmer(r ~ 1 + (1|study),
                          data=counts,
                          offset=log(e),
                          family=poisson,
                          refresh=0,
                          seed=4356,
                          prior_aux=cauchy(0,1,FALSE),
                          prior=normal(0,1,autoscale=FALSE),
                          prior_intercept=normal(0,1,autoscale=FALSE),
                          prior_covariance=decov(1, 1, 1, 1/3)
                          )

The following Stan model should match, but it does give different results:

data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=0> r[N];
  vector[N] offset;
}
parameters {
  real beta;
  vector[N] eta;
  real<lower=0> tau;
}
model {
  r ~ poisson_log(beta + tau * eta + offset);
  eta ~ normal(0, 1);
  tau ~ exponential(3);
  beta ~ normal(0, 1);
}
generated quantities {
  real tauSq;
  tauSq = square(tau);
}

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: Confusion in glmer poisson models
parts:
Did you forget to exponentiate your linear predictor, i.e.

  r ~ poisson_log(exp(beta + tau * eta + offset));

There are (at least) two places here where we have to worry about log vs linear scale; (1) the likelihood (i.e. "poisson_log" returns the log-likelihood")
and (2) the predictor (the linear predictor gives a prediction on the *log*-density scale)

  I'm a Stan newbie, so I may be barking up the wrong tree.

  Ben Bolker

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Confusion in glmer poisson models
parts: On Tuesday, March 28, 2017 at 9:35:27 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:

I am quite confused as to what rstnarm does when doing a Poisson log-link regression using stan_glmer.

I have written the respective Stan program as I think it should match, but it apparently does not line up.

There was a bug in the case where only the intercepts vary by group and the prior scale is not 1.0. It is fixed on GitHub now. The models are not exactly the same (in rstanarm, it estimates an extra parameter and your eta values are unscaled) but it is close considering how small the dataset is.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Ben!

Thanks much for fixing it... this model class is quite important as it is the standard meta-analysis model (to my knowledge).

My eta values are just the NCP parametrization way of the hierarchical model, not sure what else I should do in this ultra-sparse data set. So what do you mean by it being unscaled?

Also, what is exactly the model rstanarm fits? I haven't found this on the stan_glmer page where I would expect it; any other pointers?

Considering the patch you did I am a bit surprised that the binomial case also needed a fix as I thought it was ok (using essentially the same model), but I will double check that one once more.

Best,
Sebastian
